questions.stem: Pemberton Bakery, a mid-sized firm recorded cost of goods sold of $750,787 in Riverbend last year and an average inventory of $117,095. What was its inventory turnover, rounded to one decimal?
questions.explanation: Inventory turnover is cost of goods sold divided by average inventory. Here $750,787 divided by $117,095 gives about 6.4 times per year. Inverting the ratio would describe how many years of inventory are held, not turnover, and multiplying by 100 would turn a count into an unrelated percentage. A higher turnover generally means goods sell quickly and inventory is managed efficiently.
questions.hint: Divide cost of goods sold by average inventory.

options.misconception: inverts and rescales the ratio
multiplies by 100 instead of leaving a turnover count
inverts the ratio of cost to inventory

questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: Ironwood Dairy, a regional firm ships 6,663 units a year to Tarrow at an average freight cost of $12 per unit. What is the annual outbound freight cost?
questions.explanation: Total annual freight cost is the number of units shipped times the cost per unit: 6,663 times $12 equals $79,956. Adding a count to a rate is meaningless, dividing by twelve would give a monthly average, and quoting the per-unit rate alone ignores the volume. Logistics costs like this are a key input to channel and pricing decisions.
questions.hint: Multiply annual volume by cost per unit.

options.misconception: reports a monthly figure rather than the annual total
reports only the per-unit rate
adds units and per-unit cost instead of multiplying

questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: Meridian Confectionery, a privately held firm offers a limited-time discount and a free gift with purchase in Valeview to spur quick sales. Which element of the promotional mix is this?
questions.explanation: Sales promotion uses short-term incentives such as discounts, coupons and gifts to stimulate rapid purchase. Advertising is paid, non-personal messaging, public relations builds relationships and image, and personal selling involves direct interaction with a salesperson. A limited-time gift is a classic sales promotion tactic.
questions.hint: Short-term incentives to spur quick sales are sales promotion.
questions.learningObjective: identify elements of the promotional mix

options.misconception: mistakes a sales incentive for image-building communication
confuses a short-term incentive with paid mass messaging
assumes a face-to-face salesperson is required
